column2: Told to go to the world of the Vasus, he lay on the bed of arrows, awaiting the northern course, meditating on Vishnu and praising him.
When Duryodhana was grieved, Drona became commander; with the Pandava army delighted, Dhrishtadyumna was the army's lord.
A fierce battle occurred between them, enlarging Yama's realm; Virata, Drupada and others were drowned in the sea of Drona.
Duryodhana's great army of elephants, horses, chariots and foot, with Dhrishtadyumna as lord, Drona shone like Time.
When it was said "Ashvatthama is dead," Drona gave up his weapons; struck by Dhrishtadyumna's arrows, he fell to the ground.
On the fifth day, the invincible one, having crushed all the Kshatriyas, with Duryodhana grieved, Karna became commander.
Arjuna of the Pandavas — a battle occurred between them, weapon against weapon, most terrible, like the war of gods and demons.
In the battle named for Karna and Arjuna, Karna slew foes with arrows; on the second day Karna was felled by Arjuna.
Shalya fought half a day, and Yudhishthira killed him. Suyodhana, his army slain, fought with Bhimasena.
Having slain many men and others, he then spoke to Bhima; striking with a mace, Bhima felled him.
By mace he slew his younger brothers; on the eighteenth day, at night, he felled the sleeping force of the Pandavas.
The mighty Ashvatthama, with an akshauhini, slew Draupadi's sons with the Panchalas, and Dhrishtadyumna.
Then Arjuna took from the weeping, sonless Draupadi's side the crest-jewel of him by the blade-of-grass missile.
Hari revived the child burnt by Ashvatthama's missile; from Uttara's womb then was Parikshit, the king.
Kritavarma, Kripa and Drona's son — the three were freed from battle; the Pandavas, Satyaki and Krishna — seven were freed, not others.
Having consoled the afflicted women with Bhima and others, Yudhishthira, having performed the rites for the slain heroes, gave water and wealth and the rest.
Having heard from Bhishma, son of Shantanu, all dharmas that give peace — the dharma of kings, of liberation and of giving — he became king.

In the horse-sacrifice, the slayer of foes gave gifts to Brahmins. Having heard from Arjuna of the clubs and the destruction of the Yadavas, he installed Parikshit in the kingdom and with his brothers attained heaven.
He anointed Vajra, the burden-bearer of the Yadavas, in the kingdom; at Prabhasa Hari himself left his body from the divine region.
He is worshipped in Indra's world and Brahma's world by the heaven-dwellers. Balabhadra, of endless form, went to Patala and heaven.
Hari the god is imperishable, to be meditated on by meditators. Without him, the ocean flooded the place of Dvaraka.
Having performed the rites for the Yadavas, Partha gave water and wealth and the rest; the women, by the curse of Ashtavakra, who were Vishnu's wives remaining,
were again carried off through that curse by cowherds with clubs. Arjuna was humiliated; Partha grieved.
Comforted by Vyasa, he thought: "My strength was in the presence of Krishna." Coming to Hastinapura, Partha told everything
to his brother Yudhishthira, protector of men: that bow, those missiles, that chariot, those horses
were lost without Krishna, like a gift to an unlearned man. Hearing that, Dharmaraja, having installed Parikshit in the kingdom,
the wise one set out with Draupadi and his brothers, knowing the impermanence of the world, repeating Hari's hundred and eight names.
On the great road Draupadi, Sahadeva, Nakula, Phalguna and Bhima fell; the king was devoted to grief.

Mounted on the chariot brought by Indra, he attained heaven with his brothers. Seeing Duryodhana and the others and Vasudeva, he rejoiced. This Mahabharata has been told to you; whoever recites it goes to heaven.
He became an Arhat afterward and made others Arhats. Thus heretics arose, devoid of Vedic dharma and the rest.
They did deeds fit for hell and will accept from the lowest; all at the end of the Kali age will be of mixed castes.
Robbers and the ill-conducted; the Vajasaneya Veda, fifteen branches indeed, will be authoritative.
Clad in the mail of dharma and fond of adharma, barbarians in the form of kings will eat men.
Kalki, son of Vishnuyashas, with Yajnavalkya as priest, bearing weapons and arms, will destroy the barbarians.
He will establish the proper order in the four castes and in all the stages of life, the people on the path of good dharma.
Abandoning the form of Kalki, Hari will go to heaven; then the Krita age will arise as before.
The castes and stages will stay in their own duties, O best one. Thus in all kalpas and all Manu-periods
there are countless avatars, past and future. The man who recites or hears the account of Vishnu's ten avatars
has his wishes fulfilled, becomes pure, and with his family attains heaven. Thus Hari makes the order of dharma and adharma; having descended, he goes, Hari the cause of creation and the rest.
In it was born Brahma himself, the self-born, as we have heard; Hiranyagarbha, the Lord, having dwelt a whole year,
made that egg into two: heaven and earth. In the middle between those two halves the Lord created space.
On the waters he set the floating earth and the directions tenfold. There time, mind, speech, desire, anger and delight
the Prajapati created, wishing to create a creation of that form: lightning, thunderbolts, clouds, rainbows,
and birds he first created, and Parjanya from his mouth. For the success of sacrifice he made the Rik, Yajus and Saman.
The Sadhyas with them worshipped the gods; from his arm he made beings high and low. He created Sanatkumara and Rudra, born of anger.
Marichi, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Vasishtha — these seven mind-born are determined to be Brahmas.
These seven begot offspring, and the Rudras, O best one. Having divided his body in two, with half he became a man and with half a woman; in her Brahma created offspring.
Gridhrika, Shuchi and Sugriva; from them came crows and others. Horses and camels came of Tamra; Aruna and Garuda likewise,
of Vinata; a thousand serpents were of Surasa; the Kadraveyas a thousand: Shesha, Vasuki and Takshaka.
The fanged ones were born of Krodhavasha; birds of the earth and water; of Surabhi cows, buffaloes and the like; from Ira plants and grasses.
From Svasa were born Yakshas and Rakshasas; from the sage's horse-nature; from Arishta the Gandharvas; from Kashyapa the moving and unmoving.
Their sons and the rest were countless; the demons were conquered by the gods. Diti, her sons destroyed, propitiated Kashyapa,
and desiring a son to strike Indra she obtained one from Kashyapa. When she slept without washing her feet, he struck her womb.
Indra, seeking a gap, those gods became the Maruts; Shakra's helpers, forty-nine, of blazing radiance.
All this Hari, Brahma, having consecrated king Prithu, gave in order the kingdoms; Hari is lord of others.
Of Brahmins and herbs Chandra is king; of the waters Varuna; of kings Vaishravana; of the suns the lord is Vishnu.
Of the Vasus Pavaka is king; of the Maruts Vasava the lord; of Prajapatis Daksha; Prahlada lord of the Danavas;
of the fathers Yama is king; of the elements Hara is lord; Himavan of mountains; the ocean lord of rivers;
Chitraratha of Gandharvas; Vasuki of Nagas; Takshaka king of serpents; Garuda of birds;
Airavata of elephant-kings; the bull of cattle; the tiger of beasts; the plaksha lord of trees;
Ucchaihshravas of horses; Sudhanva guardian of the east; Shankhapada of the south; Ketuman guardian in the west; Hiranyaroma in the north. This is called the secondary creation.
Of Priti, wife of Pulastya, was born his son Dattoli; of Kshama and Pulaha were born Sahishnu and the Karmapadikas.
Of Sannati and Kratu came the Valakhilyas of great energy, of thumb-joint size, sixty thousand of them.
Of Urja and Vasishtha: the king Gatra, Urdhvabahu, Savana, Alaghu, Shukra, Sutapa and seven sages.
Pavaka and Pavamana were born; Shuchi was born of Svaha and Agni; the Agnishvattas, Barhishads, Anagnis and Sagnis from Aja.
From the fathers and Svadha were born Mena and Vaidharini as daughters. Himsa was wife of Adharma; of them was born Anrita (falsehood),
and a daughter Nikriti; from them Bhaya and Naraka; Maya and Vedana are their pair.
From them were born Maya and Mrityu, destroyer of beings; and Vedana bore a son, Duhkha, from Raurava.
From Mrityu were born disease, old age, sorrow, craving and anger. From Brahma, weeping, was born one named Rudra from weeping.
Bhava, Sharva, Ishana, Pashupati, O twice-born, Bhima, Ugra, Mahadeva — the grandfather named them.
Through Daksha's anger his wife Sati gave up her body; becoming Himavan's daughter she again became Shambhu's wife.
Worships beginning with bathing, spoken by Narada and others to the sages, performed by Svayambhuva and others, give enjoyment and liberation, of Vishnu and the rest.
Bha is the eye, Va the sun-missile, the queen and Shakti, Nishkubha; Soma, Angaraka, Budha, Jiva, Shukra, Shani in order,
Rahu, Ketu, Tejas, Chanda — thus in brief the worship. The seat for the form, the root, the heart-mantra and others, the attendant.
The seat of Vishnu; Vishnu of the form: Om Shrim Shrim Shridhara Hari. Hrim — this is the all-form mantra, enchanting the three worlds.
Hrim Hrishikesha, Klim Vishnu; with long vowels the heart-mantra and the rest; with all of them the fifth worship, giving victory in battle and the like.
Discus, mace, conch, pestle, sword, Sharnga bow, noose and goad, Shrivatsa, Kaustubha with the forest garland, in order.
Shrim: Shri, Mahalakshmi, Tarkshya, the teacher, Indra and the rest for worship; Sarasvati the seat, the form: Aum Hrim, Dadhi, Sarasvati.
The heart-mantra and the rest: Lakshmi, Medha, Kala, Tushti and Pushti; Gauri, Prabhavati, Durga, the Gana, the teacher and the field-guardian.
Likewise Gam to Ganapati, Hrim to Gauri, Shrim to Shri; Hrim to Tvarita; Hrim Sau to Tripura — ending with the dative and homage.
Beginning with Om, the first syllable of the name joined with a bindu, or joined with Om — these are remembered for those who repeat them from worship of all the mantras.
By homage with sesame, ghee and the rest, they give dharma, desire, wealth and liberation; he who recites the worship mantras, having enjoyed his enjoyments, goes to heaven.
Having set the Vardhani on the left and the worship materials on the right, washed with the weapon-mantra, he should place the arghya with scent and flowers.
Consciousness, the all-pervading light, with water recited upon eight times, and sprinkled with the mantra ending in "phat"; meditating on Hari on the hand, the supreme.
Dharma, knowledge, dispassion and lordship, facing the fire direction; adharma and other limbs, in the east and elsewhere, on the yoga seat.
The tortoise on the seat, Ananta, Yama, the sun and other orbs; Vimala and others in the filaments, the Anugraha in the pericarp.
Having meditated first in one's own heart, invited and worshipped in the circle: arghya, water for the feet, rinsing, honey-mixture, and again that;
bathing, garment and sacred thread, ornament, scent and flowers, incense and lamp — offerings with the Pundarikaksha vidya.
He should worship the limbs in the east and elsewhere: at the east door the egg-born, on the right the discus, mace on the north; in the corner the conch and bow.
To the god's left and right the quivers and the sword; on the left the shield; Shri on the right, Pushti on the left in front.
The forest-garland, Shrivatsa and Kaustubha, and outside the guardians of the quarters; one should worship all with their own mantras; Vishnu, at the end of the arghya.
One should worship separately and together with the limbs and seed-syllables; after repeating, circumambulating, praising and offering arghya,
one should place in the heart, meditating "I am Brahman, Hari"; "Come" at invocation, and "Forgive" at dismissal.
Thus having done worship with the eight-syllable mantra and others, one gains liberation. The worship of one form is told; hear the worship of the nine-fold array.
Placing on the two thumbs Vasudeva and Bala and the others, then on the forefingers and the rest, on the body, on head, forehead and face,
on heart, navel, secret place, knees and feet, in the middle, one should worship the east and the rest. One seat, nine-fold array, and nine seats as before.
On the nine-petalled lotus with nine forms, the nine-fold array as before; the chosen deity in the middle, then at the place one should worship Vasudeva.
Having meditated in the order of heart and so on, and worshipped each rite, one should offer eight oblations again for each rite.
Then the practitioner should give the full oblation with the ladle and the root-mantra, pronouncing it prolonged and well-voiced with the mantra ending in "vaushat."
Having prepared Vishnu's fire, he should cook the Vaishnava porridge; having worshipped Vishnu on the platform and recalled the mantras, he should cook.
In order beginning with the seat, the excellent enclosure with the limbs, having worshipped with scent and flowers, meditating on the best god of the gods;
having laid the fuel, then the two Aghara oil-streams placed in the Agni and Ishana directions, proceeding in the Vayu, Nirriti and other directions in order,
then having offered the two portions of ghee, the two eyes, south and north, and in the middle he should offer all the mantras in order of worship.
One should satisfy with ghee the forms, with a tenth part the limb-offering; a hundred or a thousand with ghee and the rest, or with fuel sticks and sesame.
Having completed the worship and ending with the oblations, having called the pure disciples who fasted and seated them in front, one should sprinkle the victims with the weapon-mantra.
Joining the disciples to the Self, bound by the bonds of ignorance and action, consciousness following the subtle body, bound with the subtle body,
having sprinkled by the path of meditation, he should purify with the air seed-syllable; then with the fire seed-syllable the creation called the egg of Brahma
one should contemplate as wholly burnt, standing like a heap of ash; flood the ash with water, and recall the world as water.
There one should then place the power called the earth-seed; the good earthly egg wrapped by all the subtle elements.
One should contemplate the egg, its arising, its support, made of it; in its middle one should think of the human form made of Om.
